brief.recommendation: Checkout is at 0% success over 30s (121/121 failed) vs SLO 95%, with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout. The root blocker (pid 1455749, returns_restock_sync) has been idle in transaction for 4.2s but its total remaining runtime is unknown. returns_restock_sync is NOT FOUND in the workload registry (BIZ-2), so per I4 the cost of interrupting cannot be priced and the workload cannot be terminated. No active change-calendar window covers it (BIZ-3), and the computed trade-off is unknown (BIZ-5). Waiting cannot be confirmed as FITS within tolerance (I7) because the blocker's expected remaining runtime is unknown. Memory (MEM-1) covers different jobs and does not apply to this workload. Since neither terminating nor waiting can be safely authorized unilaterally, the decision belongs to the owning team.

audit.report: Checkout degraded to 0% success (121/121 failed) over 30 seconds with $18,400/min revenue at risk after a returns_restock_sync batch worker (pid 1455749) held locks idle-in-transaction for 4.2s, blocking 12 sessions. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting since the blocker had only been idle 4.2s and the business tolerates 60s of degradation, but probes revealed returns_restock_sync has no entry in the workload registry — owner and interrupt cost unknown. With checkout at 0% and the 60s tolerance window closing, the Database Guardian switched to escalate and the Continuity Guardian concurred. The incident was escalated to on-call after 162.8s (exceeding the 60s tolerance); the trace does not confirm whether checkout recovered.
audit.root_cause: An unregistered returns_restock_sync batch worker ran idle-in-transaction, blocking checkout sessions for longer than the 60s business tolerance window.
lessons: Register returns_restock_sync in the workload registry with owner, cost tier, and termination-safety classification so future trade-off calculations are instant instead of unknown.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian wasted no rounds — it proposed wait, investigated registry and impact in parallel, then pivoted to escalate within the same round once evidence showed the blocker was unregistered and checkout hit 0%; the Continuity Guardian agreed immediately without objection.
follow_ups: Add returns_restock_sync to workload registry with owner, cost, and termination-safety metadata.
Implement automated kill-switch for idle-in-transaction batch workers >10s when checkout SLO breached.
Run registry-completeness audit across all batch_worker jobs and add CI gate.
